title: Torch & Trowel Field Notes
description: Articles and teaching notes about screen-free drawing, scaffolded art instruction, and helping students build real drawing skill.

items.title: Screen-Free Homeschool Art Curriculum Should Still Teach Real Skill
items.summary: What to look for when you want less screen time, less parent prep, and actual drawing progress.
items.content_text: A screen-free homeschool art curriculum should do more than keep a tablet closed. It should give the student a skill-building sequence, keep the parent from having to perform the lesson, and make practice visible.

items.title: Middle School Homeschool Drawing Lessons
items.summary: Older beginners need foundations, but they do not need lessons that feel childish.
items.content_text: Middle school and high school homeschool students need drawing lessons that feel age-respectful while still teaching line control, shape, form, proportion, and observation.

items.title: When a Student Says I Can't Draw
items.summary: A practical way to lower pressure and return attention to one useful mark.
items.content_text: When a student says I can't draw, treat it as a signal that the task feels too big. Shrink the next step to one line, one shape, or one visible correction.

items.title: Why Blank Pages Freeze Beginning Artists
items.summary: A blank page looks simple to an experienced artist. To a beginner, it can feel like being asked to solve every drawing problem at once.
items.content_text: A blank page is not actually empty. For a beginning artist, it is full of invisible decisions. Guided drawing narrows the first few decisions so the student can begin, practice one visible skill at a time, and build toward independence.
